summary: A request from SRI-ARC to network liaisons for mailbox addresses, because the NIC was about to start delivering Journal articles to users who wanted them. Delivery could be online at the NIC, by postal hardcopy, or by network mail to a home host, using FTP's mail commands.

eli5.summary: The library asked everyone where to send their mail so it could begin delivering articles directly to them.

subtitle: Asking for email addresses so the NIC can send journal articles over the network

tldr.problem: The NIC wanted to start delivering Network Journal articles to users, but needed their mailbox addresses and preferences for how they wanted to receive content.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 510 asks network liaisons at each site to collect and submit mailbox information from their users, including host name, username, and delivery preferences.
tldr.outcome: The NIC can use this information to deliver journal articles online, by mail, or directly to users' network mailboxes via FTP.

today: RFC 510 is a historical record of early ARPANET information services and has not been obsoleted. It documents how the Network Information Center began using email delivery to distribute information to network users.

sections.title: The NIC Journal Service
sections.content: The NIC (Network Information Center) at SRI-ARC was planning to begin delivering Network Journal articles to ARPANET users. RFC 510 is a request from Jim White at the NIC to network liaisons asking them to collect mailbox information from their users so delivery could begin.
sections.eli5: The network's information center wanted to send article collections to people, so it asked for their addresses.

sections.title: Three Delivery Options
sections.content:
Users could choose from three delivery modes: online delivery to the AUTHOR branch at the NIC, hardcopy delivery by postal service to their office, or network delivery to a mailbox at their home host using FTP mail commands. Users could select one, multiple, or all three modes.

Network delivery was handled using FTP's mail commands. For bulk articles, the NIC would send a pointer that allowed an FTP client to retrieve the full text from SRI-ARC, with automatic conversion from NLS (tree-structured) format to sequential form.
sections.eli5: Pick your choice: get articles online at the NIC, receive them in the mail, or have them sent to your computer through the network.

sections.title: Information Required
sections.content: Liaisons were asked to provide four pieces of information for each interested user: the user's NIC Ident number, which delivery modes they wanted, the standard host name or decimal address for delivery, and the username their host's FTP server required. The NIC would store this information in its Ident file, allowing users to manage their settings through the NLS system.
sections.eli5: The NIC asked: What's your account number? How do you want articles? Which computer? And what's your username there?
